newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ulster TV says pulls out of third TV station.
newsitem.headline: Ulster TV says pulls out of third TV station.

text.p: Ulster Television Plc said on Wednesday that it had pulled out of a third television consortium.

The group had been awarded the exclusive right to negotiate with the Independent Radio and Television Commission (IRTC) for the granting of a television programme service contract for a new national independent television channel in the Republic of Ireland.

Ulster said the group had submitted a formal Business Plan to the IRTC but some of the terms of the UTV/TV3 agreement were unacceptable to the IRTC which Ulster said regrettably it was unable to resolve to the satisfaction of all.

"Our board feels that the risks associated with proceeding with the proposal on the terms required by the IRTC would not be in the interests of either the company or the shareholders," Ulster said in a results statement.

The TV3 Consortium said the primary areas of concern were over UTV's level of control and the extent to which the association of UTV with TV3 might lead to distortions in the marketplace. It emphasised the overall viability of the project was not in question.

"In the light of this most recent development the Consortium has written to the IRTC expressing its appreciation of the IRTC's sustained efforts in the task of bringing TV3 to fruition," the TV3 consortium said.
UTV was unveiled as a substantial minority shareholder in TV3 last September.

A further one third of the shareholding was expected to be made available to institutional investors, with the rest of the equity held by the manager of Irish rock band U2, Paul McGuinness, James Morris of Windmill Lane Studios and accountant Ossie Kilkenny.
It was expected that UTV would bring to TV3 an expertise in operating the station and programme making.
